items.title: ELPIS II: stem cell therapy laromestrocel misses RVEF endpoint in HLHS infants but shows fewer major cardiac events (company update, AHA 2026 late-breaker)
items.summary: In the 40-infant phase 2b ELPIS II trial, laromestrocel injected during Stage II palliation for hypoplastic left heart syndrome did not improve 12-month RVEF, but the company reports fewer MACE (1 vs 8, P=0.043); full data are due at AHA 2026 on Nov 8 (Longeveron press release, Oct 26, 2026).
bullets: Design: randomised, double-blind, multicentre phase 2b trial with NIH/NHLBI funding (NCT04925024); 40 infants with HLHS got a single intramyocardial dose of laromestrocel (allogeneic bone-marrow MSCs) during the Glenn or hemi-Fontan, or surgery alone (1:1), followed 12 months.

Primary endpoint missed: in the 28 infants with baseline and 12-month CMR, RVEF fell by 2.6 percentage points with standard care and 3.3 with laromestrocel (adjusted difference -1.36, 95% CI -8.0 to 6.7, p=0.68).

Secondary outcomes: MACE 8 with standard care vs 1 with laromestrocel (P=0.043); total major cardiac events 22 vs 3 (rate ratio 0.16, 95% CI 0.03-0.52, p<0.001); TR events or valve surgery 5 vs 0 (p=0.066, not significant). The 1 death and 1 VAD implant were both in the standard-care arm.
Safety: the company reports no treatment-related serious adverse events through 12 months. It plans to ask the FDA for a meeting; FDA had already said RVEF alone would not be enough for approval.

Caution: company-reported, not peer-reviewed results from a small trial that missed its primary endpoint; MACE was not defined, few events, no multiplicity adjustment reported, so the secondary findings are hypothesis-generating. Full data are an AHA 2026 late-breaker on Nov 8.
items.source: Longeveron Inc. press release (GlobeNewswire), Oct 26, 2026; ELPIS II, NCT04925024
